statement: Fix the positive gapped Hamiltonian and physical target X above, a finite collection of status partitions satisfying (8.1), a typical Schmidt set satisfying (8.2), and a mean tree with metrics (8.6). There is a sequence of common auxiliary labels λk and nonzero vectors prek = πλk R (˜︁ Ω ⊗ BellCR)⊗k ∈ Sk, ∥prek∥ ≤ 1, (8.7) Here πλk R is the Schur-label projection on the R copies. These vectors are physical mean-energy eigenvectors of eigenvalue ˜︁ E0 and have label λk on both C and R. For every tree above, set N = ∥M−s prek∥, v = M−s prek/N, Edef = ⟨v, ˜︁ Hv⟩ − ˜︁ E0 ˜︁ g , ˜︁ H = 1 k k ∑︂ i=1 ˜︁ H(i) . Rough comparisons. For 0 < τ < 1/2, the upper bound below uses the prefix data (8.4): − log N2 k ≤ 2 log d∗ − log z + 2sW (︃ 2Bsh z + 2Bexc )︃ + ok(1), (8.8) − log N2 k ≥ 2sW [︃ 2S′ − C (︃ τ log d∗ + h(τ) a )︃ − C Edef τ S′ ]︃ − ok(1). (8.9) Here h is binary entropy. The lower bound does not require (8.4) or (8.5). Sharp comparisons. If (8.5) holds and a ≤ c/ √ B, with c sufficiently small in terms of c0, define gpre j,g = S(XUj,g) + S(Vj,g) − S(Yj,g), gpost j,g = S(Uj,g) + S(Uj,gYj,g) − S(Yj,g), gmax = max j,g gpre j,g . Then gpre j,g ≥ 0, and the sharp comparisons are − log N2 k ≤ 2 log d∗ − log z + 2sW [︃ ⟨gpost ⟩av + C (︃ aB + | log z| a )︃]︃ + ok(1), (8.10) − log N2 k ≥ 2sW [︃ 2S′ + (1 − τ)⟨gpre ⟩av − C (︃ τ log d∗ + h(τ) a + aB )︃ − C Edef τ (S′ + gmax) ]︃ − ok(1). (8.11) The upper sharp bound does not require (8.4). For every physical partition there is the exact identity 2SX + gpre j,g − gpost j,g = I(X : Vj,g) + I(X : Yj,gVj,g). (8.12) All replica limits are taken with the physical system, auxiliary dimensions, finite status collection and tree, a, and τ fixed. The errors are uniform over terminal probabilities, including their dependence on k, and over the symmetric vectors to which the lower comparison is applied. Constants or degrees in intermediate polynomial factors in k may depend on the fixed entire system. They disappear in ok(1). The displayed constants in the rough bounds are universal; those in the sharp bounds may also depend on C0, c0. None has additional dependence on the system dimensions.
